say: Part one. After a short greeting, say in one sentence why you are sending this. For example: I am calling about the date for Ada's naming ceremony.

panel.heading: Point, details, next step, close
items: Greeting and the main point, in one sentence
Two or three details only
The next step: what to do, and by when
A short thanks, then stop

say: Part two. Two or three facts only. If there are more, it may need a call or a typed list.

panel.heading: Point, details, next step, close
items: Greeting and the main point, in one sentence
Two or three details only
The next step: what to do, and by when
A short thanks, then stop

say: Part three. Say what you want the listener to do, and by when. Please tell me by Friday if Saturday works.

panel.heading: Point, details, next step, close
items: Greeting and the main point, in one sentence
Two or three details only
The next step: what to do, and by when
A short thanks, then stop

say: Then close with a short thanks or blessing, and stop. Do not trail off with OK, so, yes.

items: Greeting and the main point, in one sentence

The next step: what to do, and by when

say: So think for ten seconds, then put the point first.

panel.rule: Think for ten seconds, then put the point first.

say: For example, Grace in Ibadan is treasurer of her church women's group. She must tell 40 members that contributions will be due on a new date. Her first recording lasts 2 minutes 40 seconds, and the new date comes only at the end.

items: First try: 2 minutes 40 seconds, date at the end
Point: due on the 5th, not the 10th
Details: the reason in one line, same account
Next step: reply with a thumbs-up
New note: 38 seconds, date typed underneath

say: A useful photo answers a question before anyone asks it. First, light. Use daylight, with the light falling on the subject, not behind it. Avoid the flash, which makes faces flat and causes glare.

cards.d: Use daylight near a window or in open shade. Light falls on the subject. Avoid the flash.
Wipe the lens. Walk closer instead of zooming. Keep it level with grid lines. Clear the background.
Put a coin, a biro, your hand or a tape measure beside the subject to show its size.

say: Second, framing. Wipe the lens, because a fingerprint smear is the most common cause of hazy photos. Walk closer instead of zooming, keep it level, and clear the background.

cards.d: Use daylight near a window or in open shade. Light falls on the subject. Avoid the flash.
Wipe the lens. Walk closer instead of zooming. Keep it level with grid lines. Clear the background.
Put a coin, a biro, your hand or a tape measure beside the subject to show its size.

say: Third, scale. A photo alone cannot show size. Put a coin, your hand or a tape measure beside it. A tape measure is best, because it gives a number.

Put a coin, a biro, your hand or a tape measure beside the subject to show its size.

say: The fourth idea is sequence: wide, medium, close-up. For example, Bisi in Abeokuta wants a tailor 20 kilometres away to copy a dress. She hangs it near a window and takes a wide shot of the whole dress.

panel.heading: Bisi's three-photo sequence
items: Wide: the whole dress, top to hem
Medium: neckline and sleeves
Close-up: zip and pleats, with tape measure
Typed line: length 112 cm, fabric, day

say: Then a medium shot of the neckline and sleeves, and a close-up of the zip and pleats, with a tape measure across the waist.

panel.heading: Bisi's three-photo sequence
items: Wide: the whole dress, top to hem
Medium: neckline and sleeves
Close-up: zip and pleats, with tape measure
Typed line: length 112 cm, fabric, day

say: She sends them in order and types: length 112 cm, same neckline. The tailor asks just one question, instead of asking her to come in.

panel.heading: Bisi's three-photo sequence
items: Wide: the whole dress, top to hem

say: Use video only when movement, order or sound is the message. For example, Ngozi in Lugbe, Abuja, writes a shot list of four landmarks from the main road to her yellow gate.

panel.heading: Ngozi's directions video
items: Write a shot list: 3 to 6 shots
Steady phone, good light, low noise
Say what the viewer is about to see
Trim, then watch once with sound
Send with a typed address or caption

say: Her brother drives while she films from the passenger seat, holding the phone with both hands, naming each landmark as it appears.

say: Her raw video is 3 minutes 10 seconds. She trims the slow parts in her gallery editor down to 1 minute 25 seconds, and watches it once with sound.

say: She sends it with a location pin and the typed address. And remember: never film while driving. Ask a passenger to film, or stop safely first.

say: To remember. Point first, with the key fact typed underneath. Listen back before you send. Use daylight, move closer and add scale, then send wide, medium and close-up. Keep videos short and trimmed.
